claim: The official README for precise-prefix-cache-producer explicitly labels the plugin's lifecycle hooks, distinguishing '(EndpointExtractor) Per-pod ZMQ subscriber lifecycle on add/delete' from '(PreRequest) Speculative-index the selected endpoint(s) with TTL eviction' — confirming the maintainers document this plugin as implementing the EndpointExtractor interface.
stance_target: The precise-prefix-cache-producer implements the router's EndpointExtractor interface rather than the kv-cache library's own Kubernetes pod discovery
scope_conditions: llm-d-router preciseprefixcache README.md, main branch as of commit bffcfb7 (Sep 5, 2026)
quoted_support: (EndpointExtractor) Per-pod ZMQ subscriber lifecycle on add/delete.

claim: Without setting prefixMatchInfoProducerName on the paired prefix-cache-scorer, the scorer silently falls back to the auto-spawned approximate producer rather than using precise-prefix-cache-producer.
stance_target: Operational pitfalls in configuring precise routing
quoted_support: Without the prefixMatchInfoProducerName field, the scorer falls back to the auto-spawned approx producer.

claim: SGLang's KV-events currently omit extra_keys (multimodal identifiers, cache_salt), so salted requests against SGLang backends are precise-cache misses until SGLang emits extra_keys, whereas vLLM emits extra_keys with cache_salt in block-0.
stance_target: Engine compatibility limits of precise prefix-cache routing
scope_conditions: llm-d-router preciseprefixcache README.md, engine compatibility table
quoted_support: SGLang | not emitted | baked into engine block hashes but not surfaced; salted requests are precise-cache misses until SGLang emits extra_keys

claim: Block keys used for precise routing are recomputed by the EPP itself from TokenizedPrompt on both the lookup path and the KV-event ingestion path, so blockSizeTokens/hashSeed need not match the inference engine's own internal block hashing.
stance_target: Mechanics of cross-engine block-key correlation in precise routing
scope_conditions: llm-d-router preciseprefixcache README.md, Engine compatibility section
quoted_support: Block keys are recomputed by the EPP from TokenizedPrompt (tokens, model, multimodal features, cache salt) on both the lookup path and the KV-event ingestion path, using this plugin's tokenProcessorConfig. The engine's own block hashes serve only as opaque keys for the engine-to-request mapping, so blockSizeTokens/hashSeed need not match the engine.
